summary: Adds int __builtin_pulp_event_unit_read_fenced(void *, int) and void __builtin_pulp_OffsetedWritePtr(void *, void *, int), the prototypes GAP9 GCC uses. Each has its own intrinsic, linked to the builtin with ClangBuiltin, so clang's generic CGBuiltin path emits it and no clang codegen or Sema file is edited. ISel: imm offset -> p.elw / sw; reg offset -> add+p.elw / p.sw rr. The fenced intrinsic has no memory attribute plus IntrHasSideEffects, a full barrier like GCC's; OffsetedWritePtr uses the PulpWriteMemIntrinsic properties and is never dropped.

verification.asm_vs_gcc: logs/20-F016-repro/cmp: in all 17 checked instructions at -O0/-O2/-Os, same instruction and addressing form as GAP9 GCC (identical encodings where the registers match, e.g. p.elw a0,60(a0)=03c56503 and p.sw a2,a1(a0)=00c565a3). Differences: register choice; clang compresses the imm-form store to c.sw where GCC emits a 4-byte sw; p.elw writes zero when the result is unused. The fenced barrier matches GCC: stores and loads are not moved across it and loads are not reused across it (t2.c dse/cse/glob). Two calls give two p.elw, a 4x-unrolled loop gives 4 p.elw, and inside a hardware loop the p.elw stays in the loop body. OffsetedWritePtr is kept even to a dead local array.

other_errors_seen: GAP9 GCC emits an unassemblable 'p.elw a5,4100(a4)' for __builtin_pulp_event_unit_read_fenced offsets > 2047 (GCC bug, not ours; clang uses add + p.elw 0).

GAP9 GCC rejects a non-constant event_unit_read_fenced offset ('offset expected to be immediate value') unless inlining makes it constant; clang accepts it (add + p.elw), which is more permissive. Not a defect.
